Here the gate reproduces the encoded rules exactly on the deterministic subset, an internal-consistency check (faithful realization of the encoding at scale) rather than a measure of real-world generalization; it escalates 31% of traffic, and the neuro-symbolic design dominates rule-only and single-classifier ablations on the same workload. To our knowledge, AgentPay is the first framework to integrate multi-agent payment orchestration with a verified symbolic compliance gate; production validation on real LLMs and expert-labeled data remains future work. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: A Neuro-Symbolic and Blockchain-Enhanced Multi-Agent Framework for Fair and Consistent Cross-Regulatory Audit Intelligence
Abstract: Ensuring consistency, fairness, and transparency in cross-regulatory compliance has become a critical national priority as enterprises increasingly file interdependent reports to agencies such as the IRS, SEC, and DOL. However, fragmented regulatory ecosystems often lead to inconsistent filings, elevated fraud risk, and inefficient allocation of audit resources. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a unified audit-intelligence framework that integrates neuro-symbolic reasoning, blockchain-based trust management, and deep reinforcement learning within a multi-agent system. First, a neuro-symbolic consistency engine combines graph neural networks with first-order logical rules to detect subtle, cross-form discrepancies that may indicate misreporting or fraud. Second, all generated evidence trails and verification outcomes are anchored on a permissioned blockchain to ensure tamper-proof traceability and transparent regulatory collaboration. Third, a multi-agent deep reinforcement learning module dynamically allocates IRS audit resources by jointly optimizing long-term tax recovery and fairness objectives, mitigating disproportionate enforcement on disadvantaged groups or small businesses. Experimental simulations using synthetic and semi-real regulatory datasets demonstrate that the proposed system significantly improves cross-agency report consistency detection (+21.7%), enhances audit transparency, and reduces allocation bias by up to 34%. This research provides a technologically grounded pathway for modernizing regulatory intelligence, safeguarding tax bases, and supporting equitable and sustainable compliance enforcement in the United States.  © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

Title: Distance–area–IoU fusion loss for better neuro-symbolic robot manipulation
Abstract: Intersection over union (IoU) is the most popular metric for evaluating accuracy in robot manipulation. However, classic IoU loss is insufficient to maximize the value of metric in robot manipulation. There are many IoU-based loss which are designed for deep learning, incorporating penalty terms to improve upon the classic IoU loss. Moreover, these methods still encounter suboptimal performance in neuro-symbolic robot manipulation (NSMR) which incorporate both symbolic reasoning and deep learning. Therefore, to accelerate convergence speed and improve the manipulation accuracy in NSMR, this paper presented distance–area–IoU fusion (DAIoU_F) loss which combines information from both line and area dimensions of the bounding box corners. Three diverse language-guided robot manipulation datasets each containing different object and object rational language instruction have been built in this paper. DAIoU has been integrated into the latest language-guided robot manipulation neuro-symbolic operation architecture and verified on three diverse datasets. This paper achieves improvements in both the IoU metric and convergence speed within the same training period. The dataset, checkpoint and code are available in https://github.com/cher0000/language-guided-robot-. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Title: Counterfactual Enabled Neuro-Symbolic Digital Twins for Intelligent Industrial Maintenance
Abstract: Industrial predictive maintenance is a critical challenge in modern manufacturing, where unexpected equipment failures cause significant economic losses through downtime, repair costs, and disrupted production. Conventional maintenance approaches, whether reactive or schedule-based, are becoming inadequate to manage the high-dimensional sensor information of the IoT-enabled machineries. The paper presents a novel hybrid neuro-symbolic digital twin that builds upon Remaining Useful Life (RUL) estimation by combining temporal transformers, physics-informed constraints, and counterfactual reasoning. The model integrates complementary approaches into a single and interpretable predictive system. A temporal transformer backbone is a model of long-range dependencies in multivariate sensor time-series data allowing the detection of gradual patterns of degradation that are frequently overlooked by traditional models of recurrence. The learning objective contains physics-informed constraints that guarantee that predictions are consistent with the principles of thermodynamic, mechanical, and material fatigue, connecting data-driven learning to domain knowledge. A Conditional Variational Autoencoder (CVAE) produces counterfactual failure events, simulating alternative histories of operation, under hypothetical conditions. This mechanism increases data diversity, enables interpretable diagnostics, and reinforces neuro-symbolic reasoning. A method of improving maintenance policies with the help of multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL) is applied to minimize downtime, unnecessary maintenance, and equipment life. The results of the experiments on 24,042 sensor measurements of CNC machines, pumps, compressors, and robotic arms show good results. The framework has attained RMSE of 21.52 h and a 0.918 score, R2 which is 25.1 percent better as compared to the baseline models. The accuracy of prediction of failures was 94.2 percent, and the maintenance policies were optimized to achieve a reduction in equipment failures by 51.7 percent compared to the rule-based scheduling, which is based on the fact that CVAE-generated counterfactual state transitions were used to train the Q-learning agent, which indicates the practicality of the framework. Copyright © 2026 The Authors.

Title: A Reinforcement-Guided Graph Attention Framework for Autonomous Self-Healing in Software-Defined Networks
Abstract: Today’s communication networks are more complex and dynamic in nature and are frequently exposed to unexpected failures, latency spikes, and congestion caused by changing user needs and the limitations of infrastructure. Although Software-Defined Networking (SDN) brings centralized control enabling programmable network management, it also poses new risks and single points of failure. This paper presents NeuroGraph-HealNet, an end-to-end intelligent self-healing network architecture based on a hybrid of Graph Attention Networks (GATs) and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for real-time network healing and optimization. The system learns from dynamic topological states and traffic patterns and continuously adapts to autonomously identify faults, forecast degradation threats, and perform corrective actions. In contrast to conventional reactive systems, our solution includes neuro-symbolic planning to predict cascading failure and dynamically re-schedule data flows ahead of time in order to maximize packet delivery and reduce downtime. High-fidelity simulations based on Mininet and ONOS-emulated SDN settings validate enhanced resilience with 43% reduction in average recovery latency and restored throughput up to 96.5% within milliseconds after the identification of an anomaly. The envisioned NeuroGraph-HealNet not only improves service continuity as well as fault tolerance but also redefines the scalability of AI agents in mission-critical self-healing network infrastructures. ©2026 IEEE.

Title: From APIs to Semantic Agents: Evolving Enterprise Platforms through Knowledge-Driven AI
Abstract: Modern enterprise systems expose functionality through APIs, yet these interfaces remain static and unaware of business context. This paper introduces a knowledge-driven semantic agent architecture that transforms traditional APIs into intelligent, goal-oriented services by combining large language models (LLMs) with symbolic reasoning and enterprise knowledge. The framework defines a semantic contract for each API (linking all inputs and outputs to an ontology) and embeds a neuro-symbolic control loop that interprets user intent, applies domain knowledge and business rules, and dynamically plans actions. A prototype was developed in realistic e-commerce scenarios (free-form product listing and adaptive order handling) to evaluate feasibility. Methodologically, two agent-augmented API services were evaluated on 40 test cases (20 per scenario) against baseline implementations, measuring task success, policy compliance, and latency. The semantic agents consistently achieved higher success rates (∼ 90% task completion) with no observed policy violations, while introducing only a modest latency overhead of a few hundred milliseconds-well within acceptable ranges for enterprise workflows. These results demonstrate that knowledge-driven agents can significantly improve automation, adaptability, and explainability in enterprise platforms. The paper details the system architecture, implementation, and quantitative evaluation, and discusses how semantic contracts and neuro-symbolic reasoning enable 'APIs that think' in an AI-powered enterprise. © 2026 IEEE.
